name: Wallace Chiachang Kou
current_role: Founder, President & CEO, Silicon Motion Technology (NASDAQ: SIMO)
profile: Taiwanese-American engineer who founded Silicon Motion in May 1995 after senior engineering roles at Western Digital (VP/Chief Architect, multimedia products). He built it into the world's largest merchant NAND flash controller maker (SSD, eMMC/UFS controllers), and still runs it, now pushing into AI/data-center SSD controllers.
interesting_fact: Silicon Motion describes itself as the world's largest NAND flash controller vendor; its controllers sit inside a large share of the world's SSDs and memory cards.
deep_cut_fact: Kou earned his MS in electrical & computer engineering at UC Santa Barbara (1983-85); despite a weak chip market he got 20+ job offers and credits a UCSB course where students fabricated and tested real silicon. His advice to young engineers: "Don't hesitate."
notes: Low public profile; best route via Silicon Motion corporate communications (Minnie Lin) or IR. Company is relevant to AI data-center storage angle.

name: Amir Schlachet
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Global-E Online Ltd. (NASDAQ: GLBE)
profile: Israeli co-founder (2013) and CEO of Global-e, a cross-border direct-to-consumer e-commerce platform partnered with Shopify; IPO'd on Nasdaq in 2021. Before Global-e he spent 11 years in elite IDF technology units, was a McKinsey consultant, SVP/strategy adviser to Bank Hapoalim's CEO and head of e-payments at 888 Holdings.
interesting_fact: He served 11 years in elite IDF technology units, including commanding the Talpiot program, Israel's elite military science-and-technology track.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding Global-e he was VP and head of e-payments at online gaming company 888 Holdings, giving him the payments background behind Global-e's cross-border checkout model.
notes: Press requests go via Global-e's PR agency Headline Media. Sources differ on his degrees (Tel Aviv Univ. M.Sc. per company bio).

name: Rahul Gyanchandani
current_role: Joint Managing Director, RSPL Group (Ghadi detergent), Kanpur
profile: Second-generation leader of Kanpur-based RSPL Group, founded in 1988 by Murli Dhar and Bimal Kumar Gyanchandani with Ghadi detergent, now one of India's largest detergent brands. As Joint MD he fronts Ghadi's marketing (e.g. the Madhuri Dixit 'Vishwas Ki Pariksha' campaign) and launches such as Ghadi Rapid Wash liquid detergent.
interesting_fact: Beyond detergent, RSPL has diversified into dairy (Namaste India), footwear, real estate and renewable energy, operating wind and solar plants across India generating over 50 MW.
deep_cut_fact: RSPL began as Rohit Surfactants Pvt. Ltd. in 1988; in 2006 four family detergent companies, including one named Rahul Detergents Pvt. Ltd., were merged into RSPL, and Ghadi Industries was folded in in 2008.
notes: Family is known as low-profile ('silent billionaire' coverage of Murli Dhar Gyanchandani). Forbes wealth likely listed for the family; Rahul appears as company spokesperson in campaign press releases. Only general company email published.

name: Larry Eugene Allbaugh
current_role: CEO, Buzz Oates Group of Companies (Sacramento commercial real estate); Director, Five Star Bancorp (NASDAQ: FSBC)
profile: Sacramento-area real estate executive who runs the Buzz Oates Group, a major Northern California commercial real estate investment, development and management firm, and is a longtime director and >10% holder (via Buzz Oates entities) of Five Star Bancorp, parent of Rancho Cordova/Rocklin-based Five Star Bank.
interesting_fact: Five Star Bancorp's SEC filings show its large stake is held through the Buzz Oates Group of Companies, of which Allbaugh is CEO and a shareholder, making the real estate firm one of the bank's biggest owners.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Best route is via Buzz Oates corporate office (contact page). Also reported board roles at Teichert, Inc. and Vanguard University (aggregator data, unverified).

name: Vijaykumar Gupta
current_role: Promoter/founder of Gujarat Ambuja Exports Ltd (GAEL), Ahmedabad; former Chairman & Co-MD (1991-2018); no longer on the board
profile: Ahmedabad industrialist who promoted Gujarat Ambuja Exports (incorporated 1991), now one of India's largest maize/corn wet-milling, starch, soya and edible-oil processors with maize capacity of ~5,600 TPD. He chaired the company until 2018, when leadership passed to Manish Vijaykumar Gupta, now Chairman & MD; the family retains control.
interesting_fact: GAEL runs wind power projects in Gujarat and solar plants in Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, and is building into ethanol/ENA (a 180 KLPD grain-based plant in Malda, West Bengal).
notes: Very little public info on him personally; the company's public face is Chairman & MD Manish Vijaykumar Gupta. Alive status not confirmed in sources found. Not related to Ambuja Cements.

name: Toby Z. Rice
current_role: President & CEO and Director, EQT Corporation (NYSE: EQT), largest US natural gas producer
profile: Co-founded Rice Energy with his siblings (family started 2007) and served as President/COO until EQT bought it for $6.7B in 2017. In 2019, at age 39, he won a proxy fight and became EQT's CEO, turning it into a vertically integrated gas producer (Equitrans acquisition) and a vocal advocate for US LNG exports and gas to power AI data centers.
interesting_fact: He became CEO of America's largest natural-gas producer in July 2019 after leading a shareholder proxy campaign to take control of the company that had acquired his family's firm.
deep_cut_fact: At Rollins College he captained the 2004 'Dirtbags' baseball team (48-12, first Sunshine State Conference title, DII College World Series semifinal) and was SSC Player of the Year batting .376. A lesson he draws: "You can't tell if you're winning if you're not keeping score."
notes: Very media-friendly; frequent podcast/conference guest on gas, LNG and AI power demand - strong fit for an energy/data-center podcast. Media route: EQT Strategic Communications (Amy Rogers, Head of Strategic Communications, listed in 2026 releases; email not captured).
